original_final_review.summary: The current updater (sha256 73ab2454…) is logically correct. Its exact-version, idle, reviewed-hash, expectedVersion and atomic-write guards are intact. The owned-profile migration recognizes only the byte-exact prior template (a8b2198, reproduced from 5cfa2400) and its single authorized Astra-to-Sol substitution (658246, reproduced). The generated command now calls profile_state() and carries --expect-profile-sha256. Rollback restores only bytes the run still owns. The model-evaluation scope, the 27-skill convergence (upstream trees verified, including all 15 unchanged directories), the uv.lock-only exception and the hermetic Semgrep suites are all accepted. Two blocking problems remain. (1) The whole finalization is built on a stale main checkout (5cfa2400), 24 commits behind remote main cc1f6ce1. Remote main changed the same updater (#514) and tests, and 3-way merges of both conflict, so the reviewed updater cannot land unchanged. The pin, stack row and receipt id codex-01592-qualification-20260930 duplicate work on the unmerged D4 owner branch, which has a different receipt at the same path, contrary to the recorded handoff. (2) The prepared idle rollout's source checksum omits the imported scripts/codex_quota.py. Its three target files are frozen items in Gate A's window-W snapshot, with no recorded owner coordination. It is frozen to the stale-base source, and its armed state is not stated. Nonblocking gaps: unqualified 'same_remaining_native_argv' booleans, the missing finalization receipt, unrecorded final-input validator and full-suite runs, and a stale current_native_skills pointer.

findings.claim: The prepared production idle rollout guards the exact reviewed source and host inputs and preserves concurrent-owner protections.
findings.reason: idle-rollout.json lists six checksum inputs, but the updater imports scripts/codex_quota.py (sha256 fa0e3c9e…) and uses its AppServer and ProbeError for every production config/read and config/batchWrite. That module is not guarded, while adoption/pins-linux-x86_64.json, which the updater does not read, is. The three rollout targets (~/.codex/config.toml, AGENTS.md and stack-worker.config.toml) are frozen items in Gate A's window-W freeze snapshot. The W contract requires no carrier or instruction change during the run, and the rollout rewrites the Codex global instruction block (top rule now 215 words). No coordination with the Gate A owner is recorded, and the timer has no W refusal. The frozen inputs pin the stale-base lane from F1, and the run record would state catalog_commit 5cfa2400 via git_head() even though the executed source is uncommitted. The receipt says prepared_not_applied, but it does not say whether the transient retry timer is armed. 'root is still an active guarded client' reads as an armed timer that the idle guard is refusing.
findings.required_action: Keep the rollout unarmed, or disarm it and record that it is disarmed, until the rebased source from F1 is re-reviewed and re-frozen. Extend the ExecStartPre checksum set to the updater's full import closure (at least scripts/codex_quota.py) and record it. Obtain and record Gate A owner acknowledgment, or add a refusal while a W seal is active. In the finalization receipt, record the explicit armed/disarmed state, the arm and expiry times, and the exact frozen hashes.

findings.claim: The current updater preserves its exact-version, idle, source and concurrent-change guards and implements an exact owned-profile migration, a complete generated command and owned-bytes-only rollback.
findings.reason: Apply fails unless codex --version is 0.159.2, and the updater checks the context-mode start.mjs digest and requires daemon_auto_start=false. It fails while pgrep -x codex finds a process, and rollback also refuses in that case. It requires the reviewed config/AGENTS hashes, plus --expect-profile-sha256 when the state is 'migrate'. It re-checks the app-server's view before batchWrite with expectedVersion. profile_state() returns 'migrate' only for a digest in OWNED_PROFILE_SOURCES; any other differing profile fails. Apply writes a 0600 backup, journals the source, mode and replacing flag before the write, and does a hash-guarded atomic replace that preserves the file mode. Rollback restores only when current bytes equal the applied target and the backup equals the recorded prior digest; otherwise it reports a conflict and leaves the file. The generated apply command (line 822) calls plan.profile_state(). The lane sends no model/default_subagent_model keys, because owned_edits covers only lane keys. The synthetic tests cover the missing/wrong hash, unknown-custom refusal, command-line-only assertion, interrupted-journal rollback, later-writer conflict, changed-backup conflict and idle refusal. The upstream contracts match: the config writer allows only the user config, has an expectedVersion conflict path and deletes nulls; app-server refuses --profile.
findings.required_action: None for the logic. Carry it through the F1 rebase unchanged in behavior.
